title: Social News Feed
summary: Show each user a ranked feed of recent posts from the accounts they follow.
statement:
Design the home feed of a social app where users follow other accounts and see their recent posts.

Functional requirements:
- Users publish short posts that may include images.
- The home feed shows posts from followed accounts, newest or ranked first, with infinite scroll.
- New posts from followed accounts should appear within a few seconds.

Scale to assume:
- 300 million daily active users, each opening the feed about 10 times a day.
- On average a user follows 200 accounts; some accounts have tens of millions of followers.
- 50 million new posts per day.
hints: Compare building each feed when it is read with building it when a post is written. Which users break each approach?
Think about what is stored in a precomputed feed entry and how large one user's feed list needs to be.
Pagination over a constantly changing list is tricky. What cursor would you hand back to the client?
expectations: Clarifies ranking versus chronological order, feed freshness, and the media path for images.
Estimates feed read QPS (tens of thousands per second) and fan-out write volume, and notes the celebrity skew.
Discusses fan-out on write versus fan-out on read and chooses a hybrid that pulls posts from very popular accounts at read time.
Stores precomputed feeds as bounded lists of post IDs in a cache or wide-column store and hydrates post content separately.
Uses cursor-based pagination (post ID or timestamp) rather than offsets.
Serves images through object storage and a CDN, separate from the feed service.
Handles unfollows, deletions, inactive users (skip fan-out), and backfill when a user follows someone new.
